title: Gender-equality policy capacity depends on whether Pacific data systems are institutionally financed, produced, accessible and usable
source_unit: UN Women and Pacific Community, Pacific Gender Data Outlook Index 2026
geography: Pacific Island countries and territories; index evidence from 11 of 22 jurisdictions with national statistical system data available

observations.period: 2026; Pacific Gender Data Outlook Index assessment

denominator.unit: Pacific Island countries and territories in the regional frame

coverage.value: the Index includes evidence for 11 of 22 Pacific Island countries and territories

policy_infrastructure.value: gender data make inequality visible, help set policy priorities, inform resource allocation and support accountability

boundary.value: the assessment is not comprehensive because data were not available for all jurisdictions, including some populous Pacific countries

observations.method: UN Women and Pacific Community regional assessment adapted to small populations, geographic dispersion, capacity constraints and climate and economic shocks, using national statistical system responses and desk evidence.
observations.uncertainty: The regional frame and assessed subset should not be treated as a representative estimate for all Pacific jurisdictions or as a measure of gender-equality outcomes.
observations.subgroup: National statistical offices, national statistical systems, policy institutions, women and girls facing intersecting disadvantage, and communities exposed to geographic, climate and economic vulnerability.
observations.counterinterpretation: A stronger data system can improve visibility and accountability without guaranteeing political action, adequate resources or better lived outcomes.

enabling_environment.value: laws, policies, institutional mandates, gender-statistics focal points or entities, collaboration and national budget financing form the enabling environment for gender data

production.value: data production covers the ability to collect, process, integrate and produce gender statistics through surveys, censuses and administrative systems

accessibility.value: open data, dissemination and partnerships determine whether produced data can be found and used beyond the producing institution

observations.method: Index framework organized around enabling environment, data production and data accessibility, with a broader conceptual data-use dimension.
observations.uncertainty: The framework identifies institutional capacity and bottlenecks; it does not by itself establish how effectively each system changes policy or services.
observations.subgroup: Statistical offices, line ministries, data users, civil society, researchers, development partners and policy decision-makers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formal laws, focal points or open-data mechanisms can exist without sufficient staff, financing, interoperability, political independence or sustained use.

observations.period: 2026; monitoring gender-specific Sustainable Development Goal indicators

denominator.unit: gender-specific SDG data availability frame cited by the report

availability_gap.value: around 4 in 10 data points required to monitor gender-specific SDG indicators remain unavailable
availability_gap.unit: reported share of required data points

production_access_gap.value: production capacity is relatively stronger than some institutional, financing and accessibility conditions, so collecting data does not ensure that it is available for policy use

investment_signal.value: lower Index scores are intended to identify where targeted investment and strategic planning are needed

observations.method: Regional Index scoring and review of gender-data system dimensions, linked to the report's discussion of SDG monitoring gaps.
observations.uncertainty: The availability estimate is a regional reporting signal, not a causal decomposition of whether missingness comes from financing, institutional design, collection difficulty, access restrictions or political incentives.
observations.subgroup: People whose experiences are missed by weakly disaggregated data, especially across sex, age, disability, location, ethnicity, socioeconomic status and other intersecting conditions.
observations.counterinterpretation: More data are not automatically better policy; collection can impose burdens or create privacy risks, and prioritization still requires political judgment and local knowledge.

denominator.unit: global gender-data system indicators considered in the adapted methodology

adaptation.value: the methodology was adapted for Pacific small-population, dispersion and capacity conditions and uses 15 of 16 global indicators where comparable evidence was available

data_use.value: data use is part of the conceptual framework but its indicators were omitted from the final Index because comparable evidence was limited

interpretation.value: Index scores are diagnostic signals for system-strength and investment priorities, not causal estimates or a ranking of gender equality outcomes

observations.method: Adapted UN Women and Pacific Community Gender Data Outlook methodology combining direct national statistical system responses with desk review and comparable indicator scoring.
observations.uncertainty: Omitted data-use indicators, missing jurisdictions and uneven evidence limit cross-country comparability and prevent the Index from capturing the full pathway from data production to policy change.
observations.subgroup: National statistical systems and their data users, including governments, civil society, researchers, regional organizations and development partners.
observations.counterinterpretation: A transparent diagnostic can still improve coordination and investment even when it cannot measure downstream policy impact; conversely, a high score can conceal informal exclusion or weak political uptake.

related_sources.claim: UN Women publication page describing the first systematic region-wide assessment of gender-data capacity in the Pacific.
UN Women data portal providing the publication context for gender statistics, data systems and evidence use.

boundary: This record adds a Pacific institutional-data layer linking gender-data capacity to policy visibility, prioritization, resource allocation, accountability and investment decisions. It covers 11 of 22 Pacific jurisdictions with available evidence, is diagnostic rather than causal, and is not a respondent-level dataset, a complete regional census or a measure of gender-equality outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official UN Women PDF and publication page were reviewed for the 11-of-22 coverage frame, enabling-environment, production and accessibility dimensions, SDG data availability gap, adapted indicator methodology and data-use limitation.
